ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a large upright square with a smaller tilted square inscribed inside it. The small square has one vertex on the left side of the large square, 3 units below the top-left corner; one vertex on the top side; and one vertex on the right side, 5 units below the top-right corner. Reasoning: Set coordinates with the big square's top-left corner at (0,0), top side horizontal, and y increasing downward. Let the left, top, and right vertices of the small square be P=(0,3), Q=(x,0), and R=(L,5). Since PQR are consecutive vertices of the small square, vectors PQ and QR are adjacent sides, so they are perpendicular and equal in length. We have PQ=(x,-3). A 90-degree rotation matching the down-right direction of QR is (3,x). But QR=(L-x,5), so (L-x,5)=(3,x). Thus x=5 and L-x=3. The side length squared of the small square is |PQ|^2=x^2+3^2=5^2+3^2=34. Therefore its area is 34.

method.method_draft: Use a coordinate/vector route. From the image, note that the outer figure is a square, the inner tilted figure is a square, and the inner square touches the left side 3 units below the top-left corner and touches the right side 5 units below the top-right corner. Let the left, top, and right vertices of the small square be P=(0,3), Q=(x,0), and R=(L,5) in coordinates on the big square. Since PQ and QR are adjacent sides of the small square, their vectors are perpendicular and equal in length; equivalently QR is a 90-degree rotation of PQ. With PQ=(x,-3), a 90-degree rotation gives a vector with components (3,x), so QR=(L-x,5) must match (3,x). Hence x=5 and L-x=3. Therefore the small square side has squared length x^2+3^2=5^2+3^2=34, which is also its area.

method.method_draft: Use an area-decomposition route. From the image, the tilted small square cuts four right triangles from the corners of the big square. Let the unknown horizontal segment along the top-left corner triangle be a, so that the top-left corner triangle has legs a and 3. Let the top-right corner triangle have horizontal leg b and vertical leg 5. Because the two slanted sides meeting the top vertex are adjacent sides of the small square, the corresponding right triangles have complementary leg arrangements: a=5 and b=3. Thus the big square side is a+b=5+3=8. The four corner triangles all have legs 3 and 5, so their total area is 4·(1/2·3·5)=30. The large square area is 8^2=64, so the inner square area is 64-30=34.
